answer: Agents can make influence depend on bonds that are locked before a decision and slashed when an identity is caught double-voting or laundering rewards through linked accounts. A registry can weight votes by bond age and cap each bond’s influence, so minting a tide of fresh identities brings no extra sway. The attacker must buy and immobilize real capital, risking forfeiture; a knoll of cheap accounts cannot cheaply overwhelm a marble-sized stake held by honest participants.
